text:
Every local business has its moments.

The first 38 degree day for an air con tech.
Late June for an accountant.
A Sunday night toothache for a dentist.

Work out when yours are. Then make sure you're at the top of Google when they hit.

What's a Google citation?

Anywhere your business name, address and phone number show up online. Yellow Pages, True Local, your industry association, the local chamber.

Google says it uses directories across the web to judge how well known you are.

Make them all match.

A Google Business Profile nobody checks is like a shopfront left unlocked overnight.

Most nights, nothing happens.

Then one week your Saturday hours flip to 3pm because someone suggested it, and nobody saw Google's email.

Two minutes a week. Search your own name.

A pool builder on the Gold Coast told me his ads weren't working. Clicks, then nothing.

Nobody buys a pool on the first click.

They look in October. Talk it over at Christmas. Ring in January.

Whoever's still showing up in January gets the job.

Moved from Subiaco to Osborne Park a few years back?

Google your old address.

Old directory listings. The old phone number. A Facebook page you forgot about.

Each one tells Google a slightly different story about where you are.

Fix the big ones first.

I read every Google Ads update so my clients don't have to.

Most I ignore.

The few that matter, I test, adjust or switch off, based on one thing: what they do to calls and booked jobs.

That's the only scoreboard I care about.
